[Illustration]

CHAPTER ONE

The morning broke clear and cold over the little harbour town and the
fishermen went down to their boats before the sun had fully risen. Grey
gulls wheeled above the grey water and the smell of salt and tar hung
thick in the narrow streets. Old Martha stood in her doorway and watched
the men go by and thought of her own son who had sailed away that spring
and had not yet returned. The tide was turning and the wind came fresh
from the open sea and somewhere a bell rang slow and mournful across the
quiet bay. She drew her shawl about her shoulders and went inside to
tend the fire and to wait as she had waited many mornings before this
one, patient and quiet and full of a hope she could not name.

CHAPTER TWO

By noon the boats were far out upon the water and the town lay drowsing
in the pale winter light. Children played along the shingle and the
older folk sat mending nets and talking of the weather and the price of
fish. It was an ordinary day in an ordinary place and yet to Martha it
seemed that the whole world held its breath and waited with her for the
sound of oars and the sight of a familiar sail against the far horizon.
